source_text: Adiecit ad plenitudinem tam expeditae orationis, ut non de remittendis tantum, sed etiam de auertendis in totum delictis supplicaremus: NE NOS INDUCAS IN TEMPTATIONEM, id est, ne nos patiaris induci, ab eo utique qui temptat. ceterum absit ut dominus temptare uideatur, quasi aut ignoret fidem cuiusque aut deicere sit geStiens. diaboli est infirmitas et malitia. nam et Abraham non temptandae fidei gratia sacrificare de filio iusserat, sed probandae, ut per eum faceret exemplum praecepto suo, quo mox praecepturus erat, ne qui pignora deo cariora haberet. ipse a diabolo temptatus praesidem et artificem temptationis demonstrauit. hunc locum posterioribus confirmat, orate, dicens, ne temptemini. adeo temptati sunt dominum deserendo, quia somno potius indulserant quam orationi. ergo respondet clausula, interpretans quid sit, ne nos deducas in temptationem. hoc est enim: SED DEUEHE NOS A MALO.
thought_title: The final petition: deliverance from temptation and evil
orientation: Tertullian is expounding the last petition of the Lord's Prayer, after discussing the forgiveness of debts.
pass_a_gloss: He added to the fullness of so concise a prayer, that we should pray not only about sins to be forgiven, but also about sins to be averted altogether: LEAD US NOT INTO TEMPTATION, that is, do not allow us to be led, by him of course who tempts. For the rest, far be it that the Lord should seem to tempt, as if either he does not know each one's faith or is eager to cast down. Weakness and malice belong to the devil. For also Abraham he had ordered to sacrifice his son not for the sake of tempting his faith, but of testing it, so that through him he might make an example for his own precept, which he was soon going to command, that no one should hold pledges dearer than God. He himself, tempted by the devil, showed him to be the overseer and craftsman of temptation. He confirms this passage by later words, saying, pray, that you may not be tempted. To such a degree they were tempted by deserting the Lord, because they had indulged sleep rather than prayer. Therefore the closing clause answers, interpreting what it is, do not lead us into temptation. For this is: BUT DELIVER US FROM EVIL.

choices.why: The petition is quoted in Latin from the Lord's Prayer; rendered in English as the familiar petition, with temptation as the glossary term.
rejected: Do not bring us into trial
Do not lead us into testing

choices.english: do not allow us to be led
choices.why: Tertullian's own interpretation of the petition; patiaris is permissive, so 'allow' preserves the sense that God does not actively lead but permits.
rejected: do not suffer us to be led
do not let us be led

choices.english: by him of course who tempts
choices.why: utique marks the obvious agent, the devil; 'of course' keeps the rhetorical force.
rejected: by him who tempts, to be sure

choices.english: the overseer and craftsman of temptation
choices.why: Both nouns are concrete and active; 'overseer and craftsman' preserves the two distinct roles Tertullian assigns to the devil.
rejected: the president and author of temptation
the ruler and maker of temptation

choices.why: The closing petition of the Lord's Prayer; 'deliver' is the standard rendering of deuehe in this context, and 'evil' preserves the neuter malo.
rejected: But carry us away from evil
But rescue us from the evil one

choices.why: Pignora refers to children or loved ones as pledges; 'pledges' keeps the metaphor of something held dear as a token.

Abraham ordered to sacrifice his son

pass_b_english: To the fullness of this concise prayer he added that we should ask not only for sins to be forgiven, but for them to be turned away entirely: “Lead us not into temptation” (Matthew 6:13). That is, do not allow us to be led in—by him, of course, who tempts. Far be it from the Lord to seem to tempt anyone, as if he did not know each person's faith or was eager to cast them down. Weakness and malice belong to the devil. For Abraham too was ordered to sacrifice his son not for the sake of tempting his faith, but of testing it, so that through him God might make an example of his own command, which he was soon going to give: that no one should hold pledges dearer than God. When the Lord himself was tempted by the devil, he showed who is the overseer and craftsman of temptation. He confirms this point later when he says: “Pray, so that you may not be tempted” (Matthew 26:41). And they were tempted by deserting the Lord, because they had given themselves to sleep rather than prayer. So the closing petition answers and interprets what “lead us not into temptation” means. For this is what it means: “But deliver us from evil” (Matthew 6:13).
